text:
Sam: Heads-up — canary runs show a reproducible corruption when FP8 matmul + batching coalesce short and long contexts. outputs look fine with bf16 but with fp8 we get subtle token errors after ~1.2k tokens.

Maria: repro? any logs or flamegraph?

Sam: quick summary: workload is chat-like, mix of 32-token prompts and 1024-token continuations. our batching heuristic coalesces micro-batches into a single kernel with pad-aligned packing. when packing stride != cache-aligned we see what I'm calling a 'padshift' — some rows in the packed A/B appear shifted by one element under fp8 quantization path.

Jia: padshift — interesting. does it happen on single-GPU only or across pods?

Sam: single GPU (A100 v4) in dev. multi-GPU also shows it when we enable continuous batching. forcing batch size 1 avoids it.

bench-bot: Perf snapshot attached in thread (summary):
- kernel chosen: fp8_gemm_v2
- wall: 12.3ms / token (fp8 path)
- wall: 18.1ms / token (bf16 fallback)
- failure rate: ~0.4% tokens mismatch against reference bf16 after token 1200

Maria: can you paste the minimal repro command?

Sam: yeah. run in docker on dev image with these env vars:

```
ENABLE_FP8_PADSHIFT=1 \
ENABLE_CONT_BATCH=1 \
REPRO_SEQ=1248 \
python -m infra.bench.run --model rwd-7b --batcher coalesce --seed 42
```

Sam: Also dump of the matrix checksum snapshot when corruption manifests:
```
# before matmul (fp8 pack): A_crc=0x8f7c12b, B_crc=0x3a1d4e0
# after matmul:   C_crc=0x0badcafe (expected 0x0baf1dea)
# difference localized to rows 128..160
```

Jia: localized rows suggests packing index miscompute or KV offset aliasing. Did you validate packer indices vs KV writer? maybe micro-batch coalescer uses a byte offset calc that underflows on certain pad lengths.

Sam: that's my current hypothesis. I added an assert in the packer: pack_indices are monotonic and match raw offsets. assert fails intermittently when ENABLE_FP8_PADSHIFT=1.

Maria: any relation to quant calibration tables? if scale quantization boundaries sit on a rounding edge, fp8 cast might magnify an index error into a visible token delta.

Sam: right — observed that when calibration yields scale S such that S*max_elem ~ 127.5, the fp8 roundtrip flips a high bit post-gemm causing an extra token shift in softmax. But the core issue is the matrix data itself being shifted before quant.

Jia: try two experiments:
1) force packer to use 64-byte aligned stride (workaround).
2) rerun with QUANT_CALIB_MODE=static vs dynamic.

Sam: I tried (1) and it masked the bug entirely. (2) changes error frequency but doesn't remove it.

bench-bot: quick diff of kernel selection log:
```
[2026-03-17T14:12:03Z] selected kernel fp8_gemm_v2 for shapes (B=8, M=1536, K=4096)
[2026-03-17T14:12:03Z] coalesced micro-batches -> packed M=2048 stride=1536 pad=64
[2026-03-17T14:12:03Z] call matmul(fp8_gemm_v2) -> returns OK
```

Maria: sounds like packing stride derived from coalesced M doesn't account for per-request effective row lengths. If some micro-batches have been padded to different extents and we reuse a shared temp buffer without resetting tail values, fp8 quant path could read stale tail bytes.

Sam: exactly. tail zeroing fixes it too. zeroing costs ~0.3ms per call, but we can avoid if we tighten coalescer invariants.

Jia: actionables:
- add assert and unit test for packer index monotonicity (Sam)
- add tail-zero on debug builds and enable in canary (Sam)
- add regression test in perf-suite exercising short+long context coalescing patterns (Maria)
- audit quant calibration boundary conditions and add a guard for scales near half-LSB (Jia)
- add a kernel-selection check: if fp8 chosen and packing stride != cache-line multiple then fall back to bf16 (temporary safety) (Maria)

Sam: I'm also going to add a small repro harness that fuzzes micro-batch pad lengths and reports any CRC delta. putting PR up in an hour.

deploy-bot: canary rollout paused for rwd-7b fp8 path in us-west-2 until this is resolved :warning:

Maria: thanks. the likely long-term fix is to ensure packer doesn't alias tails and to teach coalescer to conservatively align when quant kernels are used. I'll schedule a deep dive tomorrow 10:30am.

Jia: also add a note to the docs: fp8 kernels require strict buffer alignment and deterministic tail handling. saved us from a handful of customer surprises.

Sam: PR: https://stash.redwood/sam/pack-fix (WIP). attaching minimal logs and crc dumps. will update when CI passes.

Maria: great, post the unit test name here when ready so I can wire it into nightly regression.

Sam: will do. thanks all.
